title: CI: a job ran over 10 minutes
thread:
**Issue #4721 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4721: CI: a job ran over 10 minutes
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[CI run 45382133214](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45382133214) on `main` (`8637328`, push) had jobs over the 10-minute alert (#73):

| Job | Time | Result |
|---|---|---|
| [rust (test tools, wasm 1/4)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45382133214/job/138414441526) | 12m 21s | success |
| [rust (test tools, wasm 4/4)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45382133214/job/138414441724) | 13m 5s | success |

Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 8-minute target, not just under the 10-minute alert, so the fix has headroom. Most splits are a count in `scripts/ci-shards.toml` (#3072): `web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)` (for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`), or a `rust (test <group>)` group, whose count runs its tests in that many jobs, split by name. A count splits the run, not the compile: a group slow to compile needs its tests in more binaries (the engine's `rules_<n>` each get a job by themselves). Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI.

Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`, and a count or a new `rules_<n>` needs no change there. When the split needs a new group or other flags in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`, or any other change under `.github/`, make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45389354274)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

`rust (test tools, wasm k/K)` finishes under the 8-minute TARGET on every shard, with headroom below the 10-minute alert. The two reported shards (`1/4` at 12m 21s, `4/4` at 13m 5s) are split away: any single test too long for one shard is daily-moved with a per-PR keeper (a count cannot split a test), and the group's shard count rises so no shard's remaining tests can fill the budget. A person applies the one pinned file the bot may not touch.

## Files to touch

| File | New/change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/ci-shards.toml` | change | `[rust-test]` `"tools, wasm" = 4` becomes `= 8`; rewrite that entry's comment paragraph (new times, issue number, why 8, pin note) |
| `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs` | change, conditional | Only if Step 4 names a test here: `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` plus a hand-written keeper that plays no games, copying the `r4607000` keeper pattern |
| `crates/tools/src/carried.rs` | change, conditional | Same treatment, only for a test Step 4 measures over the threshold here |
| `crates/tools/src/gate.rs` | change, conditional | Same treatment, only for a test Step 4 measures over the threshold here |
| `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` | person only | Builder never edits it; Step 9 hands a person the exact diff |

Must not touch: `.github/` (contingency only, person-side), `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/` otherwise, `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`, `apps/web/src/test/shardWeights.ts` (the slow jobs are Rust, not web/e2e), `spec/` (a CI split is not a rules decision, so no ruling note, no `R<n>` test, no `spec/pending/` paragraph). Governing sections: `scripts/ci-shards.toml` header, `.github/ci/rust-test.toml` `[[group]] "tools, wasm"` (lines 170–174), `.github/ci/matrix.py` `shard()`, `.github/workflows/super.yml` `daily-tests` legs.

## Steps

1. Read the four governing sources listed above plus `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` lines 25–90 (read-only; do not edit).
2. List the group's tests exactly as CI does, flags copied from the `rust-test.toml` entry:
`cargo test --workspace --exclude jackioh-engine --exclude jackioh-cards --exclude jackioh-server --exclude jackioh-ai -- --skip fuzz:: --skip selfplay:: --skip positions:: --list --format terse > /tmp/tools-wasm.txt`. Save all intermediate output under `/tmp`, never in the repo.
3. Reproduce CI's split: `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py shard 1 4 < /tmp/tools-wasm.txt` and `shard 4 4`; record both test sets. Also run `shard k 8` for k 1–8 as the preview distribution.
4. Time the suspects locally, in this order, one at a time: `fork_screen::r4397000_an_always_differing_candidate_forks_every_game_at_the_cap` (`cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- --exact <path>`), the `carried::r4382000` tests, `gate::b28_b31_the_easy_ai_wins_against_the_random_policy_and_every_game_is_clean`, then any other test in the Step 3 sets. Rule, no judgment: every test over 180 s wall time here is a daily-move candidate (a count cannot split a test, and CI runners are no faster than this box).
5. For each candidate over the threshold, daily-move it following `crates/tools/src/fork_screen.rs` lines 1591–1649 exactly: add a hand-written keeper test that asserts the same wiring without playing a game (name it `<same-ruling>_a_hand_written_<thing>_without_playing`, e.g. the existing `r4607000_a_hand_written_save_reprints_its_tally_without_playing`), document both tests' doc comments as there, and mark the live one `#[ignore = "daily: <what it plays live, seconds measured here>; <keeper name> keeps <property> per pull request"]`. The attribute must carry a `daily:` reason: the acceptance scan fails a bare `#[ignore]`.
6. In `scripts/ci-shards.toml`, change `"tools, wasm" = 4` to `"tools, wasm" = 8` (8 is `MAX_SHARDS`, the most a count may be; the web unit job already runs at 8). Replace the entry's comment paragraph with one naming #4721's times, the daily-moves from Step 5, that 8 is the cap, and that any count other than 8 needs the `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` pin changed.
7. Verify the split: `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix` must list `tools, wasm 1/8` through `8/8`; every name in `/tmp/tools-wasm.txt` must land in exactly one K=8 shard; re-time the slowest K=8 shard's tests and confirm slowest-shard run plus a warm-cache list build stays under 6 minutes locally, leaving headroom to the 8-minute TARGET. If two slow tests hash into one K=8 shard, daily-move the slower one too (Step 5) rather than re-tuning the count.
8. Run the focused checks: each new keeper plus its file's neighbors (`cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh <keeper>`), `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`. `cargo jackioh spec check` is not needed: no ruling note is added or cited.
9. Contingency, only if Step 7's compile-plus-list on a warm cache already exceeds 6 minutes (compile-bound: no count helps, since every shard recompiles). Stop, do not invent a partition: put the measured compile and slowest-shard times in the pull request description and ask a person to split the group in `.github/ci/rust-test.toml`, with the constraint that the new groups' filters partition every test into exactly one group (mirror the `tools fuzz` / `tools duos, selfplay` filter pattern).
10. Write the pull request description with a `Person-side half` section carrying the exact diff below, and ask a person to apply it (the bot may not edit `bot/`; until applied, `bot selftest` is red, which is expected and named in the PR). In `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`: the comment's `` `tools, wasm` four since #4432 `` becomes `` `tools, wasm` eight since #4721 ``; the JOBS entries `"tools, wasm 1/4", "tools, wasm 2/4", "tools, wasm 3/4", "tools, wasm 4/4",` become `"tools, wasm 1/8", "tools, wasm 2/8", "tools, wasm 3/8", "tools, wasm 4/8", "tools, wasm 5/8", "tools, wasm 6/8", "tools, wasm 7/8", "tools, wasm 8/8",`; `jobs["tools, wasm 1/4"]` becomes `jobs["tools, wasm 1/8"]`; `{(1, 1), (1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (4, 4)}` becomes `{(1, 1), (1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (4, 4), (1, 8), (2, 8), (3, 8), (4, 8), (5, 8), (6, 8), (7, 8), (8, 8)}`.

## Tests

- Each new keeper from Step 5, named `<same-ruling>_a_hand_written_<thing>_without_playing` after the #4690 example; it asserts the daily-moved test's wiring without playing games and fails if the tally/save/edge format changes.
- The daily-moved tests themselves: run once with `--ignored` to confirm they still pass (`cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- --exact <name> --ignored`), proving the daily `super.yml` legs still hold them.
- `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix` plus the K=8 shard-distribution check from Step 7 (every test in exactly one shard).
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh <keeper>`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

## Done when

- [ ] Every test over 180 s in the old slow shards is daily-moved with a playing-no-games keeper, or Step 4 measured none over the threshold.
- [ ] `scripts/ci-shards.toml` has `"tools, wasm" = 8` with the rewritten comment.
- [ ] Matrix lists eight `tools, wasm` shards; K=8 distribution holds every test exactly once; slowest shard budgets under 6 minutes locally.
- [ ] Keeper tests, `fmt`, and `clippy` pass; moved tests pass with `--ignored`.
- [ ] The PR description carries the exact `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` diff and the request for a person to apply it; the builder changed nothing under `.github/`, `bot/`, `.harness/`, or `.squishy/`.
- [ ] The contingency (Step 9) was either not triggered or handed to a person with measurements.

## Risks

- Hash collision: two remaining slow tests can land in one K=8 shard; Step 7 checks the real distribution and Step 5 removes the slower one, so no shard inherits the old 12-minute shape.
- Compile-bound group: each shard recompiles the same workspace subset, so if the warm-cache build alone fills the budget, no count suffices; Step 9 escalates to a person with numbers instead of shipping a futile bump.
- Dropped coverage: `#[ignore]` tests vanish from PR runs; the `daily:` reason plus the `--ignored` run keeps them in `super.yml`'s daily legs, and each keeper holds the wiring per PR.
- No game-logic, determinism, replay, or hidden-information risk: the change moves or shards tests only; no engine, card, AI, or view code changes.

## Open questions

- A person must apply the `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` pin from Step 10 before `bot selftest` (and hence the PR) can go green; the builder cannot do this part.
- If Step 9 triggers, a person must design the `.github/ci/rust-test.toml` group split; the builder supplies measurements but must not invent the partition.
```
